subtopics.title: How the Measurement Practice Paper Is Built and How Marks Are Won

questions.question: The measurement practice paper's topic shares are:
options: Measurement the largest share, Maps and Plans most of the rest, Probability a small handful
Finance the largest, Data most of the rest
Equal halves of Measurement and Probability

questions.question: Finance appears in the measurement practice paper:
options: Never — it belongs to the Finance paper only
In Questions Four and Five where it links directly to Measurement or Maps and Plans — costing paint, fuel, tiles

questions.question: Question Two and Question Three of this practice paper are, in order:
This paper's special demand is that:
options: Nearly every chain crosses a conversion — and the marking plan places a mark directly on the crossing

questions.question: 4 800 m and 0,25 m³, converted for two marks each:
The full-marks explanation of a 1 : 50 scale:
options: One unit on the plan represents 50 of the SAME units on the real object
The plan is 50 times bigger than the object

questions.question: Thin double lines interrupting a plan's wall are:
options: A window, drawn without a swing arc

questions.question: A bedroom wall dimensioned 2 700 mm is, in metres:

subtopics.title: Question 2: The Road Trip on the N2

questions.question: 310 km at an average 100 km/h takes:
At 6,9 litres per 100 km, the 310 km trip uses:
That fuel at R22,80 per litre costs:
4 cm on the 1 : 200 000 strip map is really:
options: 8 km — 800 000 cm down the unit ladder

questions.question: Walls of a 10 m by 7 m room, 3 m high, before openings:
Subtracting two doors (each 0,9 × 2,0) and six windows (each 1,5 × 1,0) leaves:
Two coats at 8 m² per litre requires:
Paint comes only in 10-litre tins, so the buy is:
options: 3 tins — 22,35 ÷ 10 = 2,235, rounded UP because 2 tins leaves wall unpainted

subtopics.title: Question 3.2: The Oil Drum and the Flour Boxes

questions.question: Cylinder: radius 0,4 m, height 0,9 m, pi as 3,142. The capacity is:
If the question gives a DIAMETER of 0,8 m, the marking plan's first mark sits on:
options: Halving it to a radius of 0,4 m before substituting

questions.question: Boxes 25 × 20 × 10 cm packed into a crate 100 × 60 × 50 cm:
options: 60 — 4 along, 3 across, 5 layers, and the volume check 300 000 ÷ 5 000 agrees

questions.question: Volume division alone is only a ceiling for packing because:
options: Only WHOLE boxes ship — a leftover slice along an axis fits nothing

subtopics.title: Question 4: The Plan, the Budget and the Carpenter

questions.question: 96 mm on the 1 : 50 reading room plan is really:
options: 4,8 m — and the 2-to-8-metre sanity check rings true

questions.question: A 4,8 m by 3,5 m floor with tile boxes covering 2,2 m² each needs:
options: 8 boxes — 7,64 rounded UP, because boxes are bought whole

questions.question: The east elevation is identified by:
options: Counting the openings the plan places on the east face — the door and two windows — and anchoring to compass directions

questions.question: The flooring budget line at R215,00 per box:
options: R1 720,00 — 8 × 215, the Finance link this paper allows

questions.question: The carpenter holds 6 of 240 raffle tickets. His chance of winning:
options: 1/40 = 0,025 = 2,5% — any dialect unless one is demanded

questions.question: His chance of NOT winning:
The honest sentence about repeated raffles:
options: Losing last month makes winning this month more likely
Winning is impossible after a loss
Six tickets in THIS raffle multiply his chance by six, but each new raffle starts fresh
Buying tickets never changes the chance

questions.question: A correct number in a wrong unit — 0,452 with no m³, or litres where m³ was asked — costs:
options: The answer mark — units on every line is this paper's first habit
